IRAN THREATENS “CRUSHING” RESPONSE AS U.S. READIES NEW SANCTIONS

Iran warned Friday of a “crushing” reaction to any new U.S. threats, following Washington’s pledge to unveil its most severe sanctions yet.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that further measures targeting Tehran will be revealed Monday, designed to increase economic pressure while avoiding a spike in global oil prices.

Iran dismissed the upcoming sanctions as “economic terrorism.”

As U.S. pressure mounts, restrictions on Iranian oil exports are already affecting shipments to China, sparking concerns about disruptions to global energy supplies.

UPDATE: Christian metal band Demon Hunter is suing Netflix over KPop Demon Hunters.

Formed in 2000, Demon Hunter has long toured and sold merchandise under their name—until Netflix’s animated series debuted, causing widespread confusion. Fans say the band’s identity has been undermined as people increasingly mix them up with the cartoon’s characters.

The mix-up peaked when a fan spent $500 on concert tickets, believing it was a live K-pop show tied to the series. Only after buying them did they realize it was the metal band’s tour. The fan later requested a refund.

Now, Demon Hunter is demanding that Netflix stop using KPop Demon Hunters for concerts and merchandise, citing trademark infringement. They’re also seeking damages.
